paragraphs.paragraph: The Vanity of Idols and the Greatness of God
paragraphs.title: The Vanity of Idols and the Greatness of God

answers: The way of the heathen
The way of the priests
The way of the shepherds
easy.explanation: The Lord said, “Learn not the way of the heathen.”
easy.q: Whose way were the people of Israel told not to learn?

answers: Their enemies
The signs of heaven
Famine
easy.explanation: The verse says, “be not dismayed at the signs of heaven.”
easy.q: What were the people told not to fear?

answers: A tree
A stone from heaven
A vessel of water
easy.explanation: The customs of the people are described as cutting “a tree out of the forest.”
easy.q: What was cut out of the forest to begin making an idol?

answers: They were far from the earth
They were made by human hands and could not speak
They belonged only to foreigners
medium.explanation: The idols were the work of craftsmen, could not speak, and could do neither evil nor good.
medium.q: Why could the idols not help people?

answers: Do not be afraid
Do not build
Do not speak
medium.explanation: The phrase means not to fear or be terrified by the signs of heaven.
medium.q: What does “be not dismayed” mean in this passage?

answers: Idols are ancient, but the Lord is new
Idols are beautiful, but the Lord is hidden
Idols are powerless, but the Lord is the living and everlasting King
medium.explanation: The Lord is called “the true God,” “the living God,” and “an everlasting king,” unlike powerless idols.
medium.q: What is the main contrast between idols and the Lord?

answers: They are clothed in blue and purple
They must be borne because they cannot go
They are made with silver
challenge.explanation: The idols must be carried because “they cannot go.”
challenge.q: What detail shows that idols cannot move by themselves?

answers: The Lord’s wrath
The work of the craftsmen
The signs of heaven
challenge.explanation: The verse says, “at his wrath the earth shall tremble.”
challenge.q: What causes the earth to tremble according to the passage?

answers: Human wisdom equals the Lord’s wisdom
Only the wise men of the nations know the Lord
Among all the wise men and kingdoms of the nations, there is none like Him
challenge.explanation: The passage declares that among all the wise men of the nations and their kingdoms, there is none like the Lord.
challenge.q: How does the passage describe human wisdom compared with the greatness of the Lord?

paragraphs.idea: The Vanity of Idols and the Greatness of God

answers: They will perish from the earth and from under the heavens
They will become living
They will rule over nature
easy.explanation: The message says that gods which did not make the heavens and the earth “shall perish.”
easy.q: What will happen to gods that did not make the heavens and the earth?

answers: By silver
By his power
By the hands of a craftsman
easy.explanation: The verse says, “He hath made the earth by his power.”
easy.q: By what did the Lord make the earth?

answers: Egypt
The wise men of the nations
Israel
easy.explanation: The passage says, “Israel is the rod of his inheritance.”
easy.q: Who is called the rod or tribe of the Lord’s inheritance?

answers: The Lord made the world, but the idols did not
The Lord is made of wood, but the idols are made of silver
The Lord is only on earth, but the idols are in heaven
medium.explanation: The Lord made the earth, the world, and the heavens, while the idols did not make them.
medium.q: What distinguishes the Lord from the idols?

answers: The earth or inhabited world
A small idol
A strong wind
medium.explanation: In this context, “the world” refers to the earth and its inhabited order.
medium.q: What does “the world” refer to in the statement that the Lord established it by His wisdom?

answers: Only fire and dust
Waters, vapours, lightning, rain, and wind
Only the light of the stars
medium.explanation: The Lord causes vapours to rise, makes lightning with rain, and brings forth the wind.
medium.q: Which forces of nature are attributed to the Lord?

answers: Because they were made with great wisdom
Because they were clothed in blue
Because they were made by people and had no breath in them
challenge.explanation: The graven images are false, have no breath, and are called “the work of errors.”
challenge.q: Why are the idols described as vanity and the work of errors?

answers: He causes vapours to rise, makes lightning with rain, and brings forth the wind
He builds idols, decorates them, and strengthens them
He scatters Israel and destroys its cities
challenge.explanation: This sequence comes directly from the description of the Lord’s power in verses 12–13.
challenge.q: Which sequence describes the Lord’s actions in nature?

answers: Israel is one of the idols made by people
Israel is the inheritance of the One who made all things
Israel has no connection with the Creator
challenge.explanation: After describing the Lord as the former of all things, the passage calls Israel the rod of His inheritance.
challenge.q: What is the connection between the Lord’s role as Creator and Israel’s position?

answers: Her wares out of the land
Materials for an idol
Gifts for a feast
easy.explanation: The command was, “Gather up thy wares out of the land.”
easy.q: What was the inhabitant of the fortress told to gather?

answers: New and magnificent
Spoiled, with its cords broken
Made of gold
easy.explanation: The speaker says, “My tabernacle is spoiled, and all my cords are broken.”
easy.q: How is the speaker’s tabernacle described?

answers: From the south
From the east
From the north country
easy.explanation: The passage speaks of “a great commotion out of the north country.”
easy.q: From what direction does the great commotion come?

answers: The nation’s stability
Destruction and collapse
The greatness of idols
medium.explanation: The ruined tent and broken cords portray destruction and the collapse of the community.
medium.q: What does the spoiled tabernacle represent?

answers: The sheep or people under the pastors’ care
The temple buildings
Weapons of war
medium.explanation: The flocks are those entrusted to the pastors, or shepherds.
medium.q: What does “flocks” refer to in the passage?

answers: The pastors became brutish and did not seek the Lord
The signs of heaven frightened them
There was no rain
medium.explanation: The pastors did not seek the Lord; therefore they did not prosper, and their flocks were scattered.
medium.q: Why will the flocks be scattered?

answers: Leaders who did not seek the Lord failed, and the people were scattered
The pastors built the cities of Judah
The pastors prevented the northern report from coming
challenge.explanation: The leaders’ failure to seek the Lord resulted in their lack of success and the scattering of their flocks, while the cities faced desolation.
challenge.q: What is the connection between the pastors’ failure and the destruction of Judah’s cities?

answers: That they may find it so
That they may build tents
That they may learn the customs of the heathen
challenge.explanation: The Lord says He will distress them “that they may find it so,” confirming the announced judgment.
challenge.q: Why would the Lord distress the inhabitants of the land?

answers: A stable tent, united flocks, and flourishing cities
A spoiled tent, scattered flocks, and cities made desolate
Living idols, abundant rain, and wise pastors
challenge.explanation: The passage presents a spoiled tabernacle, scattered flocks, and Judah’s cities made desolate.
challenge.q: Which combination describes the results of the calamity?

answers: Direct his own way and prepare his steps
Make silver and gold
Set up a tent
easy.explanation: The prophet says that the way of man is not in himself and that man cannot direct his steps.
easy.q: What can a person not do independently?

answers: The heathen
The Lord
The pastors
easy.explanation: The prophet prays, “O Lord, correct me.”
easy.q: From whom does the prophet ask for correction?

answers: Judgment
Mercy
Anger that could bring him to nothing
easy.explanation: He asks the Lord not to correct him in anger, lest He bring him to nothing.
easy.q: What does the prophet ask the Lord to avoid?

answers: So the correction will be measured rather than destructive anger
So the correction will have no limit
So that no one will learn anything
medium.explanation: The prophet asks for correction that is just and measured, not an anger that would destroy him.
medium.q: Why does the prophet ask to be corrected “with judgment”?

answers: Make me greater
Destroy or diminish me completely
Guide me
medium.explanation: The phrase expresses fear of being reduced or destroyed under divine anger.
medium.q: What does “bring me to nothing” mean in this prayer?

answers: The admission of human inability leads to a request for measured correction
The description of idols leads to building a tent
The northern report leads to idol worship
medium.explanation: After admitting that man cannot direct his own steps, the prophet asks the Lord for correction with judgment.
medium.q: What is the relationship between verses 23 and 24?

answers: People are completely independent
People depend on the Lord for direction and correction
People are stronger than the Lord
challenge.explanation: The prophet acknowledges dependence on the Lord both to direct his way and to correct him.
challenge.q: What does the prophet’s prayer assume about the relationship between people and the Lord?

answers: Judgment is measured correction, while anger may bring destruction
Judgment is joy, while anger is wisdom
Judgment is silence, while anger is walking
challenge.explanation: The prophet requests just and measured correction instead of destructive anger.
challenge.q: What is the contrast between “with judgment” and “in thine anger”?

answers: He rejects all correction
He accepts correction but asks that it be measured
He asks to be punished with great anger
challenge.explanation: He says, “O Lord, correct me,” but adds, “with judgment” and “not in thine anger.”
challenge.q: What attitude does the prophet express toward correction?

paragraphs.paragraph: A Plea for Judgment against Jacob’s Enemies
paragraphs.title: A Plea for Judgment against Jacob’s Enemies

answers: The heathen that did not know the Lord
Israel alone
The wise men of Judah
easy.explanation: The prophet asks the Lord to pour out His fury upon the heathen that knew Him not.
easy.q: Upon whom does the prophet ask the Lord to pour out His fury?

answers: They built his dwelling
They ate, devoured, and consumed him
They taught him the right way
easy.explanation: The verse says that they “have eaten up Jacob, and devoured him, and consumed him.”
easy.q: What did the enemies do to Jacob?

answers: The families that did not call on the Lord’s name
The pastors who sought the Lord
Those who made the earth
easy.explanation: The prayer includes “the families that call not on thy name.”
easy.q: Upon whom else does the prophet ask for judgment?

answers: They did not know the Lord and they destroyed Jacob
They built the earth and practiced righteousness
They sought the Lord and guarded Jacob
medium.explanation: The verse mentions both their failure to know the Lord and their destruction of Jacob and his habitation.
medium.q: What two wrongs are mentioned concerning Jacob’s enemies?

answers: His dwelling place
A musical instrument
A sign in heaven
medium.explanation: A habitation is a place where someone lives or dwells.

answers: They destroyed Jacob and made his dwelling desolate
Jacob built idols
Jacob failed to learn the way of the heathen
medium.explanation: The stated reason is that they devoured Jacob and made his habitation desolate.
medium.q: Why is judgment requested against Jacob’s enemies?

answers: Only a small injury
Continued destruction that brought ruin
Joy over building a house
challenge.explanation: The repeated words “eaten,” “devoured,” and “consumed” emphasize complete and continuing destruction.
challenge.q: What does the repeated description of eating Jacob emphasize?

answers: Failure to acknowledge the Lord is one reason judgment is requested
Failure to call on the Lord brings blessing to the nations
The verse makes no connection between them
challenge.explanation: The prophet includes those who did not know the Lord or call on His name among those facing judgment.
challenge.q: How is failure to call on the Lord’s name connected with the request for fury?

answers: They knew the Lord, guarded Jacob, and built his dwelling
They did not know the Lord, harmed Jacob, and destroyed his dwelling
They sought the Lord, scattered the nations, and rebuilt Judah
challenge.explanation: The verse connects their lack of knowledge of the Lord with their devouring of Jacob and desolation of his habitation.
challenge.q: Which sequence summarizes the prophet’s accusation against the enemies?

paragraphs.idea: A Plea for Judgment against Jacob’s Enemies
